C528/2187/2026
Dilip
--Applicant
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand and Others
--Respondents
Hon'ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Bhuvnesh Joshi, learned
counsel for the applicant.
Ms. Meenakshi Sharma, learned
Brief Holder for the State of
Uttarakhand.
Mr. Ashutosh Joshi, learned
counsel for respondent nos. 2 and 3.
2. The present Criminal Miscellaneous
Application has been filed seeking to
quash the charge-sheet dated
28.08.2023, the cognizance/summoning
order dated 02.09.2023, and the entire
proceedings of Special Sessions Trial No.
132 of 2023 (Case Crime No. 233 of
2023), titled State vs. Dilip, for the
offences punishable under Sections 363,
366 and 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal
Code, 1860, and Sections 5l/6 of the
Protection of Children from Sexual
Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter referred
to as the "POCSO Act"), arising out of
Case Crime No. 233 of 2023, registered
at Police Station Ranipur, District
Haridwar, pending before the learned
Additional District Judge/Special Judge
(POCSO), Haridwar, District Haridwar.
3. The prosecution case, as set out in
the First Information Report, is that the
mother of the victim alleged that her
daughter, aged about 15 years at the
relevant time, had gone to a nearby shop
but did not return home. She expressed
apprehension that the applicant had

UKHC010180372026
2026:UHC:9321
induced the victim and taken her away.
4. After investigation, the police
submitted a charge-sheet against the
applicant for the offences punishable
under Sections 363, 366 and 376(2)(n) of
the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and
Sections 5l/6 of the POCSO Act.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant
submits that the applicant and the
victim were in a relationship for several
years and that, during the pendency of
the present application, they solemnized
their marriage on 03.02.2026, after the
victim attained the legally prescribed age
for marriage. It is further submitted that
the parties have resolved their
differences and are presently residing
together as husband and wife. Learned
counsel also submits that both parties
belong to economically weaker families
and that continuation of the criminal
proceedings would adversely affect their
matrimonial life.
6. The applicant and the victim are
present in person before this Court and
have been duly identified by their
respective learned counsel.
7. Learned State Counsel opposes the
application, contending that the
allegations involve serious offences,
including offences under the POCSO Act.
However, the factum of the subsequent
marriage between the applicant and the
victim is not disputed.
8. Heard learned counsel for the
parties and perused the material
available on record.
9. The question that arises for
consideration is whether the criminal
proceedings involving allegations of
offences under Sections 376(2)(n) of the
Indian Penal Code, 1860, and Sections
5l/6 of the POCSO Act can be quashed
in the exercise of the inherent
jurisdiction of this Court in view of the

UKHC010180372026
2026:UHC:9321
subsequent marriage between the
applicant and the victim and their
present matrimonial relationship.
10. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in
Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab, (2012) 10
SCC 303, explained the scope of the
inherent jurisdiction of the High Court to
quash criminal proceedings on the basis
of a settlement, distinguishing offences
predominantly private in nature from
serious offences having a significant
impact on society.
11. Similarly, in Narinder Singh vs.
State of Punjab, (2014) 6 SCC 466, and
Parbatbhai Aahir vs. State of Gujarat,
(2017) 9 SCC 641, the Hon'ble Supreme
Court laid down the principles governing
the exercise of inherent jurisdiction in
cases involving settlements between the
parties. The exercise of such jurisdiction
depends upon the nature and gravity of
the offence, the circumstances of the
case, and whether quashing would
secure the ends of justice.
12. In the present case, it is not
disputed that the applicant and the
victim have solemnized their marriage on
03.02.2026, after the victim attained the
legally prescribed age for marriage, and
are presently residing together as
husband and wife. It is further
submitted that both parties belong to
economically weaker families and are
desirous of continuing their matrimonial
relationship peacefully.
13. Having regard to the peculiar facts
and circumstances of the case, the
subsequent marriage between the
applicant and the victim, their present
matrimonial relationship, and the
economic circumstances of both families,
this Court considers it appropriate to
exercise its inherent jurisdiction to
secure the ends of justice. In the
circumstances of the present case,

UKHC010180372026
2026:UHC:9321
continuation of the criminal proceedings
would adversely affect the matrimonial
life of the parties.
14. Accordingly, the present C-528
Criminal Miscellaneous Application is
allowed. The charge-sheet dated
28.08.2023, the cognizance/summoning
order dated 02.09.2023, and the entire
proceedings of Special Sessions Trial No.
132 of 2023 (Case Crime No. 233 of
2023), pending before the learned
Additional District Judge/Special Judge
(POCSO), Haridwar, District Haridwar,
are hereby quashed.
15. Pending application(s), if any, stand
disposed of accordingly.
(Alok Mahra, J.)
 13-10-2026
SB
